subject: SLA packaging for plan migration + credit worksheet
messages:
From: Aisha Moreno <aisha.moreno@brightcart.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.run>
Cc: ops@brightcart.com
Date: 2027-08-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA packaging for plan migration + credit worksheet

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this on. We're planning a migration from our self-hosted setup to Redwood Dedicated in Q4 and want to understand how SLA tiers and migration credits would be applied. Two quick asks:

- Can you share a worksheet that shows how a migration credit would amortize across the first three months under our expected usage (avg 300M tokens/mo)?
- We need clarity on escalation coverage — what hours and response times map to the standard vs. premium bundles, and what the price deltas are.

We are targeting a 12-month committed contract but want to pilot a subset of production traffic first. Can we also get an appendix draft we can send to procurement?

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Moreno
Head of Cloud Ops, BrightCart

Attachments: billing_report_Jun-Jul.csv
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.run>
To: Aisha Moreno <aisha.moreno@brightcart.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.run>
Date: 2027-08-04T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging for plan migration + credit worksheet

Hi Aisha — great to hear about the migration plan.

I've attached a Migration_Credit_Worksheet (Excel) that walks through several scenarios: 3-month migration credit (percentage-based), flat-month credit, and an incremental pilot discount for month one. Quick notes:

- For 300M tokens/month we modeled three uptime bands: 99.9 (standard), 99.95 (business), 99.99 (enterprise). Migration credit examples assume a 20% credit applied to Dedicated unit rates for the first 90 days, stepping down to committed rates thereafter.
- Escalation coverage: standard includes business-hours triage + next-business-day root-cause analysis; premium adds 24/7 on-call and guaranteed 1-hour initial response for Sev 1.

Vanessa — can you populate the sheet with the exact unit rates for each band and a sample DocuSign appendix? Karthik, tagging you for escalation coverage language — customers often ask for explicit on-call hours and escalation path.

Proposed next step: 30-min call tomorrow 10:00 PT to review the worksheet. Does that work?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Migration_Credit_Worksheet.xlsx
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.run>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.run>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.run>
Date: 2027-08-04T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: prelim pricing notes for BrightCart

Evelyn/Karthik — jotting down numbers to drop into the worksheet before the call.

- Unit rates (Dedicated): $0.0009/token for baseline (99.9), $0.0011/token (99.95), $0.00135/token (99.99). These reflect reserved capacity discounts at 12-month commit.
- Migration credit options: 15% flat for months 1–3 (conservative), 25% flat for months 1–2 + 10% month 3 (aggressive), or $50k one-time credit applied as invoice reduction.
- Escalation add-on: $12k/mo for 24/7 on-call + guaranteed 1-hr initial response (SLA Premium). Includes up to 10 high-severity incidents triaged per year; additional incidents billed at $1.5k/incident.
- Pilot discount: 40% off unit rate for pilot traffic (up to 10% of total tokens) for first 30 days.

I'll prep a clean appendix with the price table and sample fallback policy language. Evelyn — we should make a clear formula in the sheet so procurement can validate math quickly.

— Vanessa
VP, Commercial Ops
From: Aisha Moreno <aisha.moreno@brightcart.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.run>
Cc: ops@brightcart.com, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.run>
Date: 2027-08-05T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging for plan migration + credit worksheet

Thanks — the worksheet looks useful. Quick clarifying questions before tomorrow's call:

1) On the migration credit options, can you show an explicit amortization column that reduces committed spend before calculating the monthly unit rate? Procurement insists on seeing net ARR impact.
2) For escalation add-on: is the $12k/mo a flat pass-through or does it scale with committed throughput? We anticipate seasonal peaks and want sanity checks on cost at +50% usage.
3) Pilot discount: can the pilot window be extended to 60 days if we commit to a broader rollout at day 45?

We want the appendix to be minimally legal (high-level terms) and leave detailed billing mechanics for the SOW. If you can attach an appendix draft to the call invite, I'll circulate to procurement and legal.

Best,
Aisha
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.run>
To: Aisha Moreno <aisha.moreno@brightcart.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.run>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.run>
Date: 2027-08-06T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging for plan migration + credit worksheet — draft appendix

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the questions — answers inline and attached is a draft SLA Appendix (SLA_Appendix_draft.pdf) plus a link to a delegated DocuSign envelope for approvals.

1) Amortization: attached worksheet now includes 'Net ARR Impact' column; migration credit is applied as an invoice-level credit in months 1–3 before calculating committed spend for billing purposes. Example included for your 300M tokens scenario.
2) Escalation pricing: the $12k/mo is a flat fee for the add-on up to the committed throughput. If usage exceeds committed token thresholds by >30% in a single month, the escalation fee is subject to a usage surcharge equal to 5% of incremental spend for that month (we've added a table showing surcharge tiers).
3) Pilot window: we can set a 60-day pilot with the pilot discount (40%) provided you execute the 12-month commitment by day 45 of the pilot. We'll add a clause that allows a one-time extension to 75 days by mutual written agreement.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/anchor/0a1b2c3d — envelope 'BRIGHT-4521 SLA Appendix'

Next steps:
- I'll send the DocuSign envelope for signature once you confirm the pilot cadence.
- Evelyn/Vanessa — please mark the worksheet with the final numeric scenario and prepare the invoice wording for procurement.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Appendix_draft.pdf
